dream.title: Dream · The anthill
pages:
As a child, Hugo watched his parents argue across the road.
His ice lolly melted over his hand. The adults had no time for sticky problems.

An ant hole beside Hugo’s shoe.
The ants were dragging a shell too big for the entrance. Nobody gave way. A familiar family atmosphere.

Hugo stamped down.
The entrance filled with mud.

At least one argument had been resolved.

Knocking beneath Hugo’s sole.
Once. Again.

He tried to lift his foot. It did not move.
dream.journalBody:
Hugo dreamed of stamping on an ant hole as a child. The knocking continued after he woke.
Dream and reality divided the work: one underfoot, the other next door.
dream.fallbackPage: The sound beneath Hugo’s shoe has not stopped.

knowledge.ancientBody:
Hugo adjusts the telescope on the fifth-floor roof. Stars bend along a curve.
The curve moves too.
Hugo lets go of the focus ring. His other hand takes longer.
knowledge.windowBody:
Hugo remembers a window on the third floor opposite. The sheet is still hanging there. The window is gone.
He writes it down. The architect can explain later.

telescope.title: Telescope
telescope.nightOnly:
Hugo adjusts the focus. The daylight glare reveals one thing: the lens needs cleaning.
Try again tonight.
telescope.wrongDay:
Hugo can see a clothes rack and the eaves blocking the sky.
The focus ring cannot move a building.

After finishing his observation notes, he can press F to pack the telescope and take the stairs from the fourth-floor corridor to the fifth-floor roof.
telescope.gainedSuffix: His hand is shaking. Can he still draw the edge?
telescope.repeatSuffix: That edge again. He could try drawing it.

firstLoop.news:
The Will Circus arrives Friday. Organizers confirm that all animals have been accounted for.

Miyazaki Sushi opens its 101st branch tomorrow. The first hundred customers receive a commemorative lunch box.

Police advise residents not to give the Triangle Church their address, photograph or hair.

The observatory expects a visible supernova tonight. There is no cause for alarm. Please stop calling the weather hotline.
firstLoop.flyer:
Cover the windows. Lights off.
Unplug the television.

Added with another pen: do not look up to find it.
firstLoop.dayOneCaption: 401 adds another board. Hugo is still in slippers. A clear difference in preparedness.
firstLoop.startledCaption: The hammer stops. Hugo’s prepared complaint cannot find an opening.
firstLoop.boardingCaption: Hugo notices the last nail is bent. The tenant leaves it. Each man lets one thing go.
firstLoop.chapterText:
Hugo moves his eye away from the telescope.
The roof is still quiet. Hugo is not prepared to vouch for that quiet.

bedroom.title: Writing on the desk
bedroom.body:
Carved: the stars did not move. The eye did.
Dust deep in the grooves. Not fresh.

corridor.title: Under the wallpaper
corridor.body:
The boards will not stop it. I just do not want to see it again.
That wallpaper is years old. When was this written?

balcony.title: Seven marks
balcony.body:
Six upright. A seventh across them. Below: do not count.
Too late.

evidence.title: Old observation records
evidence.body:
Three months of star positions, clouds and times. Electricity bill worked out in the corner.
Hugo’s handwriting. The overdue notice recognizes me too.

evidence.title: Balcony telescope
evidence.body:
A chip in the focus ring. Tape on the north leg matches the old records.
Apparently Hugo used to take this seriously.

evidence.title: The leaflet
evidence.body:
Cover windows. Lights off. Unplug the TV.
Added: do not look up to find it.
The pen went through the paper.

evidence.title: Boards over 401
evidence.body:
Even the cracks are covered. The last nail is bent.
Definitely not decorative.

evidence.title: Local bulletin
evidence.body:
The Will Circus arrives Friday. Organizers confirm that all animals have been accounted for.

Miyazaki Sushi opens its 101st branch tomorrow. The first hundred customers receive a commemorative lunch box.

Police advise residents not to give the Triangle Church their address, photograph or hair.

The observatory expects a visible supernova tonight. There is no cause for alarm. Please stop calling the weather hotline.

evidence.title: Rooftop observation
evidence.body:
Hugo adjusts the telescope on the fifth-floor roof. Stars bend along a curve.
The curve moves too.
Hugo lets go of the focus ring. His other hand takes longer.

evidence.title: The opposite window
evidence.body:
Sheet still there. Window gone.
What if Hugo misremembers the sheet?

evidence.title: Writing on the desk
evidence.body:
Carved: the stars did not move. The eye did.
Dust deep in the grooves. Not fresh.

evidence.title: Under the wallpaper
evidence.body:
The boards will not stop it. Hugo just do not want to see it again.
That wallpaper is years old. When was this written?

evidence.title: Seven marks
evidence.body:
Six upright. A seventh across them. Below: do not count.
Too late.

evidence.title: Water-change label
evidence.body:
The label says to change the water on Sundays. The last tick is Hugo’s.
The fish are still fish. A useful thing to write down, apparently.

evidence.title: An eye in the tank
evidence.body:
On day three, Hugo finds an extra eye in the tank. It speaks.
The foil triangle might finally have a use.

evidence.title: Cabinet water stain
evidence.body:
Day five. Stain higher than its hand.
It offered to pay. No payment details.

Day six. Says it is 001. Says Hugo wrote that number.
Cannot find it in the book.

evidence.title: Missing pages
evidence.body:
Two torn stubs. Saturday on both sides, same crossed-out number.
Since when was Hugo’s memory that good?

evidence.title: Dust under 403
evidence.body:
Chair scrapes inside. Stops when Hugo knock. Dust under the door undisturbed.
Hope the floor just carries sound.

evidence.title: Note from 401
evidence.body:
Knock twice if you need something.
Come alone.

The note is taped low. Hugo bends to read it. His knees complain first.

evidence.title: The neighbor’s warning
evidence.body:
The tenant told Hugo to go inside, close the windows and leave the television off.
He did not say why.

deductions.title: An astronomy habit
deductions.body: Marks in the records match the telescope. Apparently Hugo bought it for more than dust.

deductions.title: A sketch through glass
deductions.body: Lens-edge marks on the sketch. A telescope view. Not proof of what is in the sky.

deductions.title: I went looking
deductions.body:
Nobody made me look. Hugo knows how to focus it.
Does not mean Hugo knows what Hugo saw.

deductions.title: What did he know?
deductions.body:
Warning first. Bulletin later.
If he meant the astronomy item, why not say so?

deductions.title: Sealing the door
deductions.body:
Sent me home. Boarded up his own door.
At least it was not just a way to shut me up.

deductions.title: Blocking the view
deductions.body:
Boards cover every crack. The writing says it does not want to see.
Could be a coincidence. Do not speak for him yet.

deductions.title: An extra tenant
deductions.body:
Hugo changed the water. Now something in it talks.
The label tracks water changes, not move-in dates.

deductions.title: Out before?
deductions.body:
Stain higher than its hand. Next day it is outside.
Maybe it was out earlier. Maybe Hugo spilled the water.

deductions.title: Another reader
deductions.body:
It knows the book. Pages missing.
Ask. Do not start by shouting.

aquarium.promptDay3: E  Speak to the thing in the tank
day3Pages:
Hugo stops at the tank. An extra eye inside.
The water-change label has no record of this tenant.

“Hand off.”
Hugo looks at his hand on the lid.
“You first. Out of my fish tank.”

No answer from the water.
Hugo puts the fish food away. The landlord will not cover feeding the wrong thing.
day5Pages:
Two fingers hold the cabinet open.
Hugo pushes. Something pushes back.

“Lend me a towel.”
“Get out of my cabinet first.”
“Hence the towel.”

The water stain is above the handle now.
It rubs the mark with its thumb. Some paint comes off.

“The landlord will keep the deposit.”
“Put it on my bill.”

Easy for it to say.
day6Pages:
It stands outside the tank. A small puddle on the floor.
Hugo walks around it.

“What do I call you?”
“001.”
“You have numbers?”
“You wrote it.”

It looks toward the bedroom.
“Stop leaving that book open.”
Hugo remembers closing it.

“How long are you staying?”
It rests a hand on the tank.

Hugo starts working out the water bill.
aquarium.question: Hugo asks: have you been reading my book?
aquarium.answerGap:
“With pages torn out like that, do I need to?”
It withdraws its hand.
aquarium.answerDefault:
“You left it on the desk.”

Not an answer.
aquarium.offer:
Hugo looks at the eye in the water, then at the foil.
The neighbor’s one-sentence instructions are proving more useful than most manuals.
aquarium.throwFoil: F  Drop the foil triangle into the tank
aquarium.sealedBody:
Hugo drops the foil triangle into the water. The eye retreats behind the weeds. The extra fingers disappear with it.
The filter keeps humming.

Hugo does not reach in to check. Today he has learned when to stop.
aquarium.offerBefore:
The fish swim between the weeds, occupied with being fish.
Hugo feels the foil triangle in his pocket. The neighbor said it could go in water. He neglected to say why.

Hugo can try it now, or keep it.
aquarium.sealedBefore:
Hugo drops the foil triangle into the tank. It sinks behind the weeds.
The fish swim away. The filter keeps humming.

No applause. Fish rarely handle that part.

ending.title: BAD END · JUST A MINUTE
lines: Hugo remembers the way. His body does not keep up.
While Hugo rests on the stairs, the fire reaches the third floor.
This time Hugo does not get up.
ending.summary:
{0} loops. Stamina limit: {1:0.#}.
Journey ended and saved.
ending.confirmWarning: Restarting clears this journey, including collected knowledge.

cult.sound:
Three more blows next door.
Hugo turns over. 401 has apparently not scheduled a day off.
dayOne:
“Go back inside.”

Hugo has not said hello. The neighbor has already planned his day.

“Renovating?”
The tenant hides the hammer behind his leg. The head sticks out. Uncooperative tool.

“Stay in today. Leave the television off.”
Hugo looks at his keys. He came to complain, not collect house rules.

No explanation.
“Windows too.”
The door closes. Hugo’s complaint remains undelivered.
cult.note:
Knock twice if you need something.
Come alone.

The note is taped low. Hugo bends to read it. His knees complain first.
door:
“Who?”
An eye appears in the crack first.

“402. Hugo. Yesterday you—”
“I know about yesterday.”

The eye checks Hugo’s hands.
Hugo shows his keys. His only available credentials.

“Take it. Do not unwrap it. It can go in water.”
A foil triangle squeezes through.

The door shuts before Hugo can ask what it is for.
End of instructions.
cult.refusal:
Someone inhales behind the door. Then silence.
Hugo waits. A complete silence. No contribution required.
cult.itemBody:
Several folds of foil. Hugo squeezes it. Something hard inside.
The neighbor said not to unwrap it. So far, a manageable instruction.

morning.wake:
Hugo is awake. The hammer next door is not finished.
The alarm clock has lost its job. The neighbor has not.
morning.neighbor:
Hugo should check on the neighbor first.
At this rate, the wall might get into the corridor before he does.
morning.food: Hugo should go home and find something to eat first.
morning.kitchen:
Hugo needs to check the fridge first.
Complaints do not count as breakfast. Even this many.
morning.fridgeOpen:
Hugo opens the fridge. A few slices of bread. Half a carton of milk.
Behind him, the television comes on.
morning.afterNews:
Hugo has a few news items to get through first.
The remote is missing. The television has plans of its own.
morning.sofa:
Hugo wants a short rest on the sofa first.
A dependable plan. It has never once ended on schedule.
morning.nap:
Hugo lies on the sofa. Something hard is under the cushion.
He leaves that problem for the Hugo who wakes up.
morning.desk:
Hugo wants to write today down at the desk first.
One less way to deny it tomorrow.
morning.writing:
Hugo opens the notebook and writes the date.
The pen tears the paper. The first official record of his day: a hole.
morning.telescope:
Hugo should check the balcony telescope first.
Now that there is a notebook, some evidence would be useful.
morning.investigate:
Hugo recognizes the old calibration marks.
Press R to record the observation.
morning.connect:
Hugo still has two records to connect.
Esc closes this page; B opens the board. Link the old records and telescope, mark it tentative, then confirm the deduction.
morning.journalBody:
Hugo woke to the hammer in 401. The tenant told him to close his windows, stay inside, and leave the television off.
Hugo went in. The television switched itself on. He ate some bread and slept on the sofa until evening.

The neighbor probably would not applaud this level of compliance.
morning.breadMeal:
Hugo eats a few slices of bread and shuts the fridge.
No accompaniments. The bread raises no objection.
morning.fridgeEmpty:
Hugo checks the fridge again, then closes it.
The bread has not grown back. A necessary investigation.
morning.sofaFree:
Hugo can rest here and let some time pass.
The sofa guarantees a place to sit. Quality of rest is not covered.

worldEnd.title: BAD END · BUSINESS AS USUAL
lines: On the seventh day, they are still charging for parking downstairs.
Fire climbs out of the drains. Someone reaches for the hydrant. Their arm coils twice before it gets there.
The broadcast tells everyone to remain indoors. When the announcer takes a breath, another voice carries on.
Hugo never went up to the roof. The stairs are gone now.
worldEnd.summary:
Day Seven. The world ends.
Hugo never saw what was above it.

rooftop.up: E  Take the stairs to the fifth-floor roof
rooftop.down: E  Return to the fourth floor
rooftop.carry: F  Pack the telescope for the roof
rooftop.carried:
Hugo folds the tripod. It is heavier than it looked from the sofa.
The stairs are at the west end of the fourth-floor corridor.
rooftop.placed: Hugo sets the tripod on the mat. Five floors, three legs, one reasonably level patch of concrete.
rooftop.missing: Hugo needs his telescope from the balcony. F packs it away.
rooftop.observe: E  Look through the rooftop telescope
rooftop.daylight: Hugo finds the far side of the city. Daylight has left very little room for stars.
rooftop.firstNight:
A bright point over the rooftops. Hugo checks the time against the bulletin.
For once, the television appears to have got something right.
rooftop.revelation:
Hugo turns the focus ring. The stars bend around something that does not fit inside the lens.
It moves.
Hugo stops adjusting. A little late to pretend he was looking for weather.
rooftop.title: Above the fifth floor
